correctness.rationale: For \(2<p<\infty\), the published global profile gives \(J(\ell_p,t)=2^{1-1/p}\) for \(t\le p\) and \(J(\ell_p,t)=2^{1-1/t}\) for \(t\ge p\). For \(t\ge p\), taking \(y=x\) attains the global upper bound at every unit vector. For \(t<p\), the balanced two-coordinate vector attains the global value, while the coordinate vector reduces exactly to one parameter \(a=|y_1|\); strict Clarkson inequality for \(a<1\), direct endpoint evaluation at \(a=1\), power-mean monotonicity, and compactness yield a strict smaller maximum. The proof handles all quantifiers and the zero-argument conventions; finite computation is only supplementary.

value.rationale: The exponent \(t=p\) is an intrinsic phase boundary in the global \(\ell_p\) James-type profile. Identifying it as exactly the threshold for base-point independence gives a complete natural classification for the newer pointwise invariant on a canonical non-Hilbert model space, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a routine recomputation.
